statement: The exact Collatz cycle condition, as a statement about the word. Over ℤ the affine identity of CollatzBridge.lean holds for every integer start (word_affine_int, two_pow_mul_iter_add_one_int: 2^d (C^d x + 1) = 3^o (x + 1) + evenCharge w, with shortcutZ x = x/2 on evens and (3x+1)/2 on odds and parityWordZ its word), so on every integer cycle (x + 1)(2^d - 3^o) = evenCharge w (cycle_equation_int); in ℕ, for a positive cycle of length d >= 1, (x + 1)(2^d - 3^o) = evenCharge w and hence 2^d - 3^o divides the even-step charge of the word (cycle_equation, cycle_dvd). CONVERSELY (cycle_of_equation): a start whose parity word w satisfies (x + 1)(2^d - 3^o) = evenCharge w with 3^o <= 2^d returns after d steps. So an integer cycle with word w exists exactly when the rational x_0 = wordConst w / (2^d - 3^o) is an integer whose parity word is w -- and the second condition is automatic, by Lagarias 1990 (lagarias-1990-rational-cycles): every word is the parity vector of exactly one rational with odd denominator, periodic under the map. That last step is not in Lean; it is checked computationally on 190069 minimal certificates (lengths <= 26) and 654279 expanding survivors (lengths <= 24), every one of whose rational cycles follows its own word and returns. PREFIX BOUND (prefix_bound_of_min): if the orbit has not dropped below x by step j then (x + 1)(2^j - 3^(a_j)) <= evenCharge (prefix), so at a cycle minimum every contracting prefix caps x + 1 by the prefix's own rational cycle value evenCharge/(2^j - 3^(a_j)) -- the exact form of Terras's 'all sufficiently large members drop' and the reason a cycle word at its minimum is a minimal certificate up to the delta exceptions of J-collatz-walk-charge-constant: it contracts only at the end, so its length is A020914(p) = the binary length of 3^p, a classical constraint (the lengths where M_d != 0, the empty-window theorem, once more). WHAT THIS IS: the cycle side of the bridge made exact -- Collatz positive cycles are minimal certificates of Paper B carrying an integer rational cycle, and the open problem is which minimal certificates have 2^K - 3^p | evenCharge w with quotient at least 2 (the trivial cycle is OE with quotient 2). Not a kill, not a bound, not a halt theorem.

The Collatz walk charge, in natural numbers. Define evenCharge on words by evenCharge [] = 0, evenCharge (even :: w) = 3^(oddCount w) + 2 evenCharge w, evenCharge (odd :: w) = 2 evenCharge w -- in closed form the sum over even positions i of 3^(o - a_i) 2^i with a_i the odd letters before i. Then (wordConst_add_two_pow) wordConst w + 2^|w| = 3^(oddCount w) + evenCharge w, so the odd-step constant and the even-step charge differ exactly by the multiplier gap; (two_pow_mul_iter_add_one) for every start x and depth d, 2^d (C^d(x) + 1) = 3^o (x + 1) + evenCharge (parityWord x d): conjugating the odd step by z = x + 1 makes every correction come from an even step; (three_pow_mul_add_one_le) hence 3^o (x + 1) <= 2^d (C^d(x) + 1), the Collatz lower envelope, the mirror of power_bound_word with the inequality reversed because the +1s only push up; (cycle_even_charge) on a cycle, (x + 1) 2^d = (x + 1) 3^o + evenCharge w, i.e. the surplus (x_0 + 1)(2^K - 3^p) IS the even-step charge of the word -- the Collatz counterpart of Paper A's finance inequality n log n (3^o - 2^L) <= L 3^o, as an identity rather than a bound; (trivial_cycle_charge) the trivial cycle 1 -> 2 -> 1 has word OE, charge 2 and (1+1)(4 - 3) = 2, by decide +kernel. Read with 2^(-h_i) = 2^i/3^(a_i) 2^(-d)... precisely evenCharge w / (2^d) = 3^o sum over even steps of 2^(-h_i) up to the factor 3^o/2^d, this is the exact form of the statement whose analytic version is J-collatz-walk-charge-constant. Compiles with no sorry; standard axioms. Priority: the z = x + 1 conjugation of the odd step is classical (Simons-de Weger's up-run formula); the even-step reading of the affine constant is likely in Halbeisen-Hungerbuehler 1997's parity-word functional; not checked beyond Hercher 2023, which does not use it. Not a bound, not a halt theorem.

Paper A's walk charge transfers to Collatz cycles as an effective, m-independent bound, and it improves the constant of Hercher 2023 Theorem 27 by four percent without moving the period bound. SETTING: a nontrivial shortcut cycle of length K with p odd steps and minimum x_0 > K - 1; alpha = log2(3/2); h_j = a_j alpha - e_j the walk height before step j (a_j odd and e_j even steps so far); delta = log2(1 + K/(x_0 + 1 - K)); H(p) = sum_{a<p} 2^(-frac(a alpha)); N_delta(p) = #{a < p : frac(a alpha) >= 1 - delta}. PROOF SKETCH. From J-collatz-even-step-charge-identity, x_j + 1 = 2^(h_j)(x_0 + 1 + S_j) with S_j = sum over even steps i < j of 2^(-h_i) >= 0, so x_j + 1 >= 2^(h_j)(x_0 + 1) for every j (no minimality needed). Minimality x_j >= x_0 gives 2^(h_j) >= (x_0+1)/(x_0+1+S_j), and S_j <= K/(1 - K/(x_0+1)) by induction, so h_j >= -delta. Since h_j = a alpha - e with e an integer, e <= floor(a alpha + delta), hence h_j >= frac(a alpha) unless frac(a alpha) >= 1 - delta, in which case h_j >= frac(a alpha) - 1 >= -delta. So sum over odd steps of 2^(-h_j) <= H(p) + N_delta(p), and with 1/x_j <= 2^(-h_j)/(x_0 + 1 - 2^delta): SUM OVER ODD CYCLE ELEMENTS OF 1/x <= (H(p) + N_delta(p))/(x_0 + 1 - 2^delta), hence Lambda_C = K log 2 - p log 3 = sum over odd steps of log(1 + 1/(3x)) <= (H(p) + N_delta(p))/(3 (x_0 + 1 - 2^delta)). This is Paper A Theorem 5.4's hug-word extremality on the Collatz side: the odd steps of the hug word sit exactly at the heights frac(a alpha), and the transport deficit of Theorem 5.3 is zero because the +1 only pushes up. CONSTANTS (COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED). H(p)/p -> 1/(2 log 2) = 0.7213475 by equidistribution; sup over p >= 100 of H(p)/p is 0.72839 (at p = 121), over p >= 10^4 it is 0.72156, and H(10781274)/10781274 = 0.72134755; by Koksma the deviation at Hercher's p = 72057431991 is below 1e-9 (the partial quotients of alpha sum to 150 through q = 5.4e12), and N_delta(p) <= p delta + 151 with delta = 2.06e-10 at Hercher's floor 695 * 2^60, so p delta < 15. On the non-dropping prefixes of sampled orbits the height inequality has no violation. COMPARISON. Hercher 2023 Theorem 27 (read from the JIS PDF) bounds the same sum, sum over the odd elements of 1/n, by (3/4) K/X_0 with K his odd count and X_0 <= every element, via Lemma 26's averaging over at most three consecutive ascending runs; both bounds are effective and hold for every m, and since every nontrivial cycle has p > 7.2e10 the comparison is 0.7213 against 0.75 on the same quantity. Hercher's Remark 28 threshold for reaching K > 1.375e11 odd steps, 2836 * 2^60, becomes 2728 * 2^60. WHAT IT DOES NOT DO: the smallest finance survivor at 2^68 and at 2^71 stays 114208327604 (margin 1.33 at 2^71), so the published period bounds are untouched; Hercher's Corollary 29 (X_0 >= 1536 * 2^60 suffices, by tracking residue classes modulo powers of two for five weeks of computation) and Barina 2025 use 2-adic information this bound ignores and remain far stronger. Priority checked against Hercher 2023 only, which averages locally and takes no rotation-orbit average; Simons-de Weger 2005 and Hercher-Puchert 2018 were not read for this constant. Not a kill, not a period bound, not a halt theorem.

The height-only bound of J-collatz-walk-charge-constant is sharp, so composing the rotation-orbit average with Hercher's per-run averaging (Lemma 26 of Hercher 2023) gains nothing: the two read the same slack and the rotation average is its sharp reading. ARGUMENT (EXACT — HUMAN PROOF). The hug word with p odd letters -- the lowest non-negative walk, odd exactly when the height is below 1 -- has its odd steps at the heights frac(a alpha), a = 0..p-1, alpha = log2(3/2), so its odd-step sum of 2^(-h) is H(p) = sum_{a<p} 2^(-frac(a alpha)) by construction. Terras's bijection realises it: exists_residue_of_word (CollatzBridge.lean, the surjective half of image_parityWord) gives r < 2^K with parityWord r K equal to the hug word, and every x_0 = r mod 2^K follows it. Along a member x_0 far above 2^K the orbit stays above x_0 and x_j + 1 = 2^(h_j)(x_0 + 1 + S_j) with S_j <= K, so x_0 sum_{odd} 1/x_j = H(p)(1 + O(K/x_0)). Hence any bound on the odd reciprocal sum that uses only x_j + 1 >= 2^(h_j)(x_0 + 1) and x_j >= x_0 is at least H(p)/(x_0 + 1) up to O(K/x_0^2), and Hercher's (3/4) K/X_0 is a weaker evaluation of that same information, not a different source of it. NUMBERS. x_0 * sum_{odd} 1/x_j / H(p) = 1.000000000000 at p = 12, 53, 300, 665 (K = 19, 84, 475, 1054) with x_0 = r + 2^(K + 300), exact rational arithmetic; the realised residues are below 2^K and the orbits follow the hug word letter for letter. CONSEQUENCE. Further improvement of the Collatz finance constant needs information the heights do not carry: the residue classes modulo powers of two of Hercher's Corollary 29, or the exact closure (x_0 + 1)(2^K - 3^p) = evenCharge w (J-collatz-even-step-charge-identity), which requires 2^K - 3^p to divide the even-step charge of the word. Not a kill, not a period bound, not a halt theorem.

The Collatz and Juggler cycle gaps are mirror images of one linear form. With x = log 2/log 3, a Collatz cycle needs 2^K > 3^p and its least gap is Lambda_C(K) = K log 2 - floor(K x) log 3 = log 3 * frac(K x); a Juggler cycle needs 3^o > 2^L and its least gap is Lambda_J(L) = ceil(L x) log 3 - L log 2 = log 3 * (1 - frac(L x)); hence Lambda_J(L) = log 3 - Lambda_C(L) for every length (one line; checked to 50 digits at the recorded lengths). The admissible sets are the two one-sided Bohr sets {frac(K x) small} and {1 - frac(L x) small} of the rotation by x, disjoint by sign, and the convergent denominators of x alternate between them (the classical alternation of convergents; sides verified by comparing the integers 3^p and 2^q below 2e7 and by frac at 80 digits above): Juggler side 19, 84, 1054, 50508, 176251, 16785921, 85137581, 357638239; Collatz side 8, 65, 485, 24727, 125743, 301994, 17087915, 272500658, 630138897. Every laboratory cycle length is Juggler-side; Eliahou's generators 301994 and 17087915 are Collatz-side and 85137581 is Juggler-side, which is why it enters Eliahou's lattice only with a coefficient that keeps the sum positive (b >= 1). Paper D's dangerous fans, 176251 + k*301994 for k <= 54 closed by the partial quotient 55 and 16785921 + k*17087915 closed by 4, are the Juggler-side set between consecutive convergents, and each closes exactly at the next Collatz bound: 176251 + 56*301994 = 17087915. The laboratory already carried the sign disjointness internally as J-the-cycle-staircase-split-is-a-sign-condition and the fan structure as J-cycle-period-bounds-are-one-semiconvergent-family and PeriodFamily.lean; this row gives them their Collatz names (Eliahou 1993; Halbeisen-Hungerbuehler 1997; Tempkin-Arteaga 1997 at a higher floor). CONSEQUENCE AND CAUTION: knowing one side never kills a length on the other (the sets are disjoint), and the CYCLE-LEVEL dictionary is x_min <-> n log n (per valley 1/x_i exact against 1/(n_i log n_i)), a different map from the walk-level log x <-> log log n of J-juggler-is-collatz-one-exponential-up; substituting one for the other is wrong by a factor n. Two recorded sentences are imprecise in this light and should be corrected where they are quoted: juggler_cycle_finance.md's 'Juggler per-step defects are relatively O(1/x) in logarithms, versus O(1) for Collatz' compares a relative with an absolute size (both maps lose O(1) absolutely and O(1/state) in the logarithm; the real difference is the extra 1/log n in the walk coordinate), and hercher-2023's note calling the even-letter count e 'the analogous valley count' (Theorem 3.31 bounds even letters by a census; Hercher bounds local minima by a Diophantine argument; the Juggler m-cycle problem is open for every m, including m = 1). Not a bound, not a kill.

The sign flip on cycles is the sign of x, and Juggler's cycle words are the words of Collatz's negative cycles. On the negative integers the odd step is |x| -> (3|x| - 1)/2, so the correction pushes |x| below the pure multiplier -- Juggler's sign -- and the cycle equation (x + 1)(2^d - 3^o) = evenCharge w >= 0 with x + 1 < 0 forces 2^d < 3^o: neg_cycle_expanding, a cycle of the ℤ shortcut map at x <= -2 of positive length has an expanding word, beside cycle_contracting for positive cycles and cycle_itinerary_formally_expanding for Juggler. At the element of least |x| the prefixes are non-contracting EXACTLY, with none of the delta exceptions of the positive side (neg_prefix_noncontracting: the even steps only subtract, so an expanding multiplier is the only way to stay away from zero), so a negative Collatz cycle word is an expanding survivor: precisely Paper A's CycleMin word shape, prefixNoncontracting and exponentExpanding, as one Lean statement (neg_cycle_word_is_juggler_shape, instantiated at -17 by neg_seventeen_word_is_juggler_shape with neg_seventeen_is_least by decide); and the finance survivors of the negative-cycle problem at a floor are the Juggler-side dangerous lengths (J-cycle-gaps-are-mirror-images, J-negative-cycle-finance-is-the-juggler-mirror). THE THREE KNOWN NEGATIVE CYCLES, in Lean by decide: -1 with word O (neg_one_cycle), -5 with word OOE (neg_five_cycle), -17 with word OOOOEOOOEEE (neg_seventeen_cycle), whose lengths 1, 3, 11 are Juggler-side lengths (the convergent numerators 1 and 3, and the semiconvergent 11 = 7 + 4 of Paper A's Remark 3.32 table). THE -17 WORD INHABITS PAPER A'S CycleMinShape (neg_seventeen_inhabits_cycleMinShape): seven odd and four even letters, 2^11 < 3^7, starts OO, ends E with an empty last odd run, length 11 -- so Paper A's floor-free Theorem 3.22, every Juggler cycle has at least four even letters and period at least eleven, is met with equality by a word that Collatz realises as an integer cycle at -17. The Juggler-specific parts of CycleMin (the floor-power realisation, the next-square inventory that lifts e >= 4 to e >= 8 at minima >= 300) are not claimed for Collatz; this is the word-level shape only. CENSUS (COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED): every expanding survivor of length <= 24 (654279 words) has a negative rational cycle following its word, and the integral ones are exactly the three families O^k, (OOE)^k, (OOOOEOOOEEE)^k -- the -1, -5, -17 cycles known since the 1970s (Lagarias 1985 Section 2) and no other, to that length. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE BRIDGE: the Juggler no-cycle problem is the word-level twin of the Collatz negative-cycle conjecture (only -1, -5, -17), not of the positive one; both need expanding survivor words whose corrections point down, and Collatz has three integer solutions where Juggler has none known. Not a kill, not a period bound, not a halt theorem. NOTE 2026-09-19: CollatzBridge.lean now defines the shortcut map locally and is a layer module of Paper A's barrel; decidedAtResidues_card and neg_seventeen_inhabits_cycleMinShape live in the auxiliary CollatzBridgeLab.lean, same namespace, outside the barrel.

IN LEAN for the uniform constant (CollatzBridge.lean, kernel-checked): two_mul_evenCharge_le, on any word with no contracting prefix 2 evenCharge w <= (|w| - o) 3^o, an induction on the word carrying the prefix condition with an offset; neg_cycle_finance, at the least element of a negative cycle 2 (|x| - 1)(3^o - 2^K) <= (K - o) 3^o, from the cycle equation; neg_seventeen_finance instantiates it (4448 <= 8748). The hug-word constant and the survivor table remain computational. Carried by Paper A Section 5.9 (Theorem 5.19 and Remark 5.20). Paper A's finance, read on Collatz's negative integers, with its walk charge on the even steps. A negative cycle of the shortcut map with least |x| = y >= 2, length K and o odd letters has, by the cycle equation (cycle_equation_int) and the exactness of its word shape (neg_prefix_noncontracting), (y - 1)(3^o - 2^K) = evenCharge w = 3^o * sum over even steps i of 2^(-h_i), h_i = a_i log2 3 - i the height before the step; since the height after an even step is still non-negative, every h_i >= 1, and for the e-th even step h >= ceil((e+1)/alpha) alpha - e in [1, 1 + alpha), alpha = log2(3/2), attained by the hug word. Hence, with theta_J(K) = 1 - 2^K/3^o and m = K - o even letters: y - 1 <= m/(2 theta_J) uniformly, and y - 1 <= H_E(m)/theta_J with H_E(m) = sum_{e<m} 2^(-(ceil((e+1)/alpha) alpha - e)), H_E(m)/m -> 1/(6 alpha log 2) = 0.41105 (0.411053 at m = 10^5). This is Theorem 4.4 of Paper A on the other side of the linear form -- |x| - 1 in place of n log n, the even letters charged at 2^(-h) in place of the floor losses -- and the survivors at a verification floor Y_0 (all |x| <= Y_0 known to enter a known cycle) are the Juggler-side dangerous lengths. COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED, by the three-gap walk: at Y_0 = 2^40 the smallest survivor is 9538065 (uniform) or 10444047 (hug); at 2^60, 5398749415 or 6028888312; at 2^68, 72448885240 under both; at 2^71, 103768467013 under both -- each a Juggler-side length, the mirror of Eliahou's and Hercher's numbers. SANITY: the -5 cycle, whose word OOE is a hug word, attains the hug bound exactly (bound 5.000 at |x| = 5); -17 sits inside it (27.1 against 17); -1 is the all-odd word with no even step. WHAT IS MISSING: no published verification floor for the 3x-1 map was found (OEIS text records, Roosendaal's index; the loops page it links was unreachable), so the table is conditional on the floor and no period bound is claimed; if the 3x-1 map is verified to 2^68 the smallest possible fourth negative cycle has length 72448885240. Not a kill, not a halt theorem, and not a claim about Juggler orbits: the Juggler side of the same inequality is cycleMin_finance, already recorded. FLOOR SUPPLIED (20 September 2026): the 3x-1 map is verified to 2^44 (J-negative-floor-makes-the-mirror-unconditional), where the smallest survivor is 16483927 under both constants, so a fourth negative cycle of shortcut 3x+1 has period at least 16483927 unconditionally; the 2^40 entry of the table above, 9538065 uniform and 10444047 hug, is the value at that floor, and the 2^68 entry stays conditional. PRIOR ART (20 September 2026, search from the laboratory machine): this survivor table is Table 2 of Sinisalo, On the minimal cycle lengths of the Collatz sequences (Oulu preprint, 2003+; sinisalo-2003-collatz-minimal-cycle-lengths) -- the same lengths, our K his n and our o his k, with his Crandall-type bound R = 1/(3 - 2^(K/o)) reproduced here to five digits on our rows; the even-charge bound above is sharper by one or two rows at each floor (his smallest surviving length 3800179 at 2^38, 9236071 at 2^40, 16181933 at 2^44 against 4404167, 9538065, 16483927). He reports no verified floor. The only published verification statement found for 3x-1 is OEIS A037084's unattributed 'up to at least 100000000' (oeis-A037084); Simons 2007 proves the 3x-1 function has exactly one nontrivial 2-cycle, at 17, with no verification floor -- de Weger's bound on 3^K - 2^(K+L) leaves nine (K, L) pairs and Steiner finishes them (simons-2007-inductive-two-cycles-3x1, read in full on 20 September 2026); his method stops at m >= 3, where the floor-based Simons-de Weger template applies and the 2^44 floor is the missing input. Paper A's Remark 5.20 cites Sinisalo, Simons 2007 and de Weger, and states the 2^44 floor with its bound, since the revision of 20 September 2026.

Paper A's cycle finance, read on the Collatz side with x_min in place of n log n, reproduces the published Collatz period bounds. For a shortcut Collatz cycle of length K with p odd steps the exact identity K log 2 - p log 3 = sum over odd steps of log(1 + 1/(3 x_j)) (Eliahou's inequality (2), Hercher's Theorem 16; KNOWN) gives Lambda_C(K) = log 3 * frac(K x), x = log 2/log 3, p = floor(K x), and x_min <= p/(3 Lambda_C). Enumerating the survivors of that bound exactly by the three-gap walk of the rotation by x (cross-checked against a float-filtered exhaustive scan below 3e7): at floor 2^40 the smallest survivor is 17087915 with 10781274 odd steps, all 13869 survivors below 4e8 lie in 301994 a + 17087915 b + 85137581 c with b >= 1 and a c = 0, and every pure multiple of 301994 is excluded (its bound is 9.85e11 < 2^40 = 1.10e12 for every multiple) -- Eliahou 1993 exactly, including why the minimum is 17087915 and not 301994; at floor 695 * 2^60 and at 2^68 the smallest survivor is 114208327604 with 72057431991 odd steps -- Hercher 2018's bound, quoted as 'more than 7.2e10 odd numbers'; at 2^71 the first two survivors are 114208327604 and 217976794617, the second being Barina 2025's bound, which removes the first by a sharper averaging this inequality does not contain. ON THE JUGGLER SIDE the same walk with Theorem 4.4 at constant 1 (n log n <= L 3^o/(3^o - 2^L)) leaves 1054 and its multiples first at floor 10^6 and 50508 first at 3.5e8; Paper A's certified comparison (Lemma 4.4b: evens charged at n^2, climb interiors at n^(3/2); paper_a_audit.survivors) is sharper and leaves 25781 and 176251, the printed finance floors of Theorem 4.6 and Corollary 5.11, every one of its survivors being a constant-1 survivor. So the inequality that matches the published Collatz bounds is the WEAKER of the two Juggler forms: the Collatz literature's finance layer sits at the level of Theorem 4.4 and Paper A's refinements have no counterpart there. CALIBRATION: N_0 = 3.5e8 corresponds under x_min <-> n log n to a Collatz floor 6.9e9 = 2^32.7, the verification frontier of the early 1980s. WHAT IT IS NOT: no cycle of any length is excluded or claimed in either problem; the Collatz numbers are re-derived, not new. The 1-cycle length 9809721694 (a Juggler-side convergent numerator, 6189245291 odd letters) survives Juggler finance at N_0 = 3.5e8 with bound 1.0e20 on n log n against a floor of 6.9e9 (OBSERVATION; the walk charge of Section 5 not applied): the numerical form of 'Juggler has no Steiner theorem', where Collatz has excluded 1-cycles since 1977 through the 2-adic run congruence k odd steps => x = -1 mod 2^k. That congruence, not a sharper inequality, is what Collatz has beyond finance, and it is exactly the missing hypothesis of J-cyclemin-closure-threshold. CORRECTED 20 September 2026 evening, both sources read: the 'sharper averaging' that removes 114208327604 at 2^71 is the final section of Hercher 2023 -- verification through 1536 * 2^60 = 3 * 2^69 suffices, by tracking residue classes modulo powers of two, his Corollary 29 -- and Barina 2025 states the consequence at his floor 2^71 = 2048 * 2^60 as a cycle length of at least 355504839929 in the standard count, which is 217976794617 shortcut steps with 137528045312 odd ones, the second survivor here; the finance alone would need 2^71.88 (p/(3 Lambda_C) = 4.36e21 for the first). Paper A's Theorem 5.18 says so since the 20 September evening edition.
